extraction.name: HELVIPAD
extraction.description: A real-world omnidirectional stereo depth estimation dataset with paired top-bottom 360° images, depth maps, and disparity maps captured in indoor and outdoor dynamic human environments, with augmented training data via depth completion.
extraction.creator: Mehdi Zayene; Jannik Endres; Albias Havolli; Charles Corbiere; Salim Cherkaoui; Alexandre Kontouli; Alexandre Alahi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data were collected on a university campus using a custom-built robot rig with two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup and an Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor, synchronized by a central processor and hardware flash trigger, across indoor and outdoor scenes under varied lighting and weather conditions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Direct measurement, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Ground-truth depth labels are sparse because LiDAR point clouds cover only a fraction of image pixels; original labels cover about 12% of pixels before depth completion.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consist of synchronized top and bottom equirectangular video frames from two Ricoh Theta V cameras and LiDAR point clouds from an Ouster OS1-64 sensor.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: LiDAR point clouds were projected onto bottom equirectangular images using optimized rotation and translation parameters; depth values were converted to disparity; an augmented training set was created via temporal aggregation, interpolation on spherical grid points, and filtering based on uncertainty and out-of-distribution thresholds.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Sequences were synchronized using a flash trigger; one out of every three camera frames was retained to match the LiDAR 10 fps rate; top images, bottom images, depth maps, and disparity maps were cropped to remove unnecessary borders and downsized from width 1024 to 512 for efficient training; unnecessary sky and ground regions were cropped in the benchmark dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Depth and disparity labels were automatically generated by projecting synchronized LiDAR point clouds onto equirectangular images; augmented labels were produced with a fully automated depth completion pipeline using temporally aggregated point clouds, interpolation, and filtering.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Projection quality was manually validated using corresponding points and pixel-wise error; average projection error was 1.7 pixels on randomly selected points and 8.0 pixels on visually challenging areas. Depth completion was validated with train/test splits of point clouds and metrics such as MAE, RMSE, MARE, Inlier Ratio, and Actual Ratio of Interpolated Points.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: LiDAR-to-image mapping optimization using BFGS; depth completion pipeline; KISS-ICP evaluated for temporal aggregation
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to support development and assessment of depth estimation methods for robotic navigation in dynamic human environments and robustness across diverse lighting conditions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is collected on a university campus and contains scene distribution differences across indoor, outdoor, and night outdoor settings; low-range distances are overrepresented due to LiDAR capturing the ground surface, and depth values decay with increasing distance because of reduced LiDAR precision.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Original depth labels are sparse due to LiDAR; depth completion is limited for fast-moving objects like cars; occlusions were not explicitly handled; object boundaries remain difficult to label precisely; indoor-trained models generalize poorly to outdoor and especially night scenes; the dataset was collected on a university campus.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of omnidirectional stereo depth estimation models; benchmarking standard and omnidirectional stereo methods; evaluating robustness and cross-scene generalization; augmented training data via depth completion is used as data augmentation.
